2	name: project-git
3	description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
4	---
5	
6	Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.
7	
8	## The model
9	
10	- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
11	  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
12	  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
13	  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
14	  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
15	  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
16	  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
17	- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
18	  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
19	  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
20	- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
21	  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
22	  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
23	  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.
24	
25	So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
26	Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).
27	
28	## Recording your work (committing)
29	
30	Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
31	`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
32	would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:
33	
34	```bash
35	# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
36	"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
37	"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
38	  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
39	
40	# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
41	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
42	    add path/to/File.lean
43	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
44	    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
45	    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
46	```
47	
48	Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
49	files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
50	anything staged in your way.
51	
52	- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
53	  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
54	  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
55	  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
56	  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
57	- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
58	  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
59	  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
60	  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
61	  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
62	  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
63	- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
64	  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
65	- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
66	  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
67	- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
68	  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
69	  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
70	- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
71	  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
72	  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
73	  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
74	  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
75	  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.
76	
77	Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
78	`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
79	make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:
80	
81	```bash
82	"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
83	```
84	
85	## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard
86	
87	Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
88	seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
89	then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
90	plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
91	The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
92	you did not ask for:
93	
94	- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
95	  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
96	  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
97	  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:
98	
99	  ```bash
100	  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
101	  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
102	  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
103	  ```
104	
105	- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
106	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.
107	
108	At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
109	since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
110	blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):
111	
112	```bash
113	"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
114	"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
115	```
116	
117	If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
118	working tree, commit once.
119	
120	## Reading history / a project's diff
121	
122	Run from the workspace root:
123	
124	```bash
125	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
126	
127	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
128	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
129	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
130	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
131	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
132	```
133	
134	Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
135	`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
136	run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:
137	
138	```bash
139	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
140	  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
141	```
142	
143	To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
144	the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
145	commit changed).
146	
147	## Caveats
148	
149	- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
150	  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
151	  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
152	  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
153	- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

/-- The adaptation's basic opens land in `d`'s unit locus. -/
lemma basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus (j : A.index) :
    (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) ≤ d.unitLocus := fun _ hw =>
  (A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j
    ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.eqn j) hw)).mp hw

/-- **The adaptation computes the unit locus**: the union of the basic opens of the
adaptation equations IS `d`'s unit locus (so the adaptation and the system cut the same
support). Uses that the pieces cover the relative curve (`exists_mem_pieces`). -/
lemma iSup_basicOpen_eqn_eq_unitLocus :
    (⨆ j, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j)) = d.unitLocus := by
  refine le_antisymm (iSup_le fun j => A.basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus j) ?_
  intro w hw
  obtain ⟨j, hwj⟩ := A.toFinCoverData.exists_mem_pieces w
  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨j, (A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j hwj).mpr hw⟩

/-- **The per-piece trace of the family support**: on the piece `D(h_j)`, the support
locus of the family is exactly `D(h_j) \ D(f_j)` — the underlying set of the colength
`Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`. This is the shape the DDR-4 finiteness argument consumes: the
piece trace of the globally closed (and, over the base, properly closed) support. -/
lemma supportLocus_inter_pieces (j : A.index) :
    d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
      = (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
        \ ((relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
  ext w
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hwj⟩
    exact ⟨hwj, fun hwb => hsupp (A.basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus j hwb)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hwj, hwb⟩
    exact ⟨fun hwU => hwb ((A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j hwj).mpr hwU), hwj⟩

/-! ## Separation is a statement about the support, not about the equations

The hypothesis `hsep` above is checkable geometrically: an overlap whose points all avoid
the family support carries a unit equation, hence a unit overlap ideal, hence a vanishing
overlap colength.  In particular an adaptation in which **at most one piece meets the
support** is automatically separated. -/

/-- **Overlaps that miss the support are separated.** If no point of `pieces i ⊓ pieces j`
lies in the support locus, then `A.eqn i` restricts to a unit there (its germ is a unit at
every point, `RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), so the overlap ideal is the unit ideal
and the overlap colength vanishes. -/
lemma subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (i j : A.index)
    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
    Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
  have hunit : IsUnit (relResAlgHom C R
      (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)) := by
    rw [relResAlgHom_apply]
    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
    intro z hz
    rw [(relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact (A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus i hz.1).mp
      (by simpa using not_not.mp (hdisj z hz))
  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ :=
    Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)) hunit
  rw [show A.ovlColength i j = _ ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j from rfl]
  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr htop

/-- **One support-meeting piece suffices.** If every piece other than `j₀` avoids the
support entirely, the adaptation is separated: any off-diagonal overlap involves a piece
missing the support, so the overlap misses it too. -/
lemma forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece (j₀ : A.index)
    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →

    ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by

  by_cases hi : i = j₀

72	unit rescaling in a single move (the `CechPic`-pattern setoid of the DD-1 spec). -/

74	  ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ d₁.cover) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ d₂.cover),
75	    ∀ x : X, ∃ u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x)ˣ,
76	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ x)).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
77	        = (u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x))
78	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ x)).op).hom (d₂.eqn x)

84	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
85	  refine ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, fun x => ?_⟩
86	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
87	  exact ⟨u⁻¹, by
88	    rw [hu, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩

90	lemma DivEq.trans {d₁ d₂ d₃ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) (h' : DivEq d₂ d₃) :
91	    DivEq d₁ d₃ := by
92	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
93	  obtain ⟨𝒱, k₂, k₃, K⟩ := h'
94	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ 𝒱, fun x => (inf_le_left (b := 𝒱.opens x)).trans (h₁ x),
95	    fun x => (inf_le_right (a := 𝒲.opens x)).trans (k₃ x), fun x => ?_⟩
96	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
97	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := K x
98	  have E1 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
99	    (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom hu
100	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E1
101	  have E2 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
102	    (inf_le_right : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom hv
103	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E2
104	  refine ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v, ?_⟩
105	  have hcast : ∀ (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x)ˣ), (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x))
106	      = w.val := fun _ => rfl
107	  rw [Units.val_mul]
108	  calc (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
109	      = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val
110	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₂ x))).op).hom (d₂.eqn x) := by
111	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
112	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x) u).val
113	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
114	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom u.val from rfl]
115	        exact E1
116	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
117	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₃ x))).op).hom (d₃.eqn x)) := by
118	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right :
119	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x) v).val
120	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
121	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom v.val from rfl]
122	        rw [E2]
123	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
124	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₃.eqn x) := by
125	        rw [mul_assoc]

129	private lemma ext_eqn {d e : X.LocalEquations} (hcov : d.cover = e.cover)

131	  cases d; cases e

138	theorem picClass_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :

140	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h

143	    refine ext_eqn rfl (heq_of_eq (funext fun x => ?_))
144	    exact (H x).choose_spec

373	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha

375	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
376	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
377	          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)

466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,

9	/-!
10	# The certificate of a support-separated adaptation
11	
12	The DD-R certificate lane was built around the equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ_left − δ_right)`
13	of the two overlap-restriction arrows.  Its two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4), and the
14	kernel-spanning input of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, are the genuinely hard
15	relative content — `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` shows the kernel-spanning law is
16	*equivalent* to the flatness one is trying to prove, so no cleverer submodule evades it.
17	
18	This file records the escape hatch that the *pointwise* gate opens up.  Because
19	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts **any**
20	adaptation over the shrunken base, we are free to choose one whose pieces are
21	**support-separated**: each off-diagonal overlap misses the divisor, so its overlap
22	colength vanishes.  For such an adaptation
23	
24	* `δ_left = δ_right` on the nose (`deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated`), hence
25	* `W(d)` is the whole product `∏_j colength j` (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'`), and
26	* both cokernels are *zero* modules, so (c3)/(c4) hold for free
27	  (`flat_coker_incl_of_separated`, `flat_coker_diff_of_separated`).
28	
29	What remains of the certificate is only the (c1) data — chart-local colengths finite
30	projective — plus the constant-rank reading of their product.  Both are already available:
31	(c1) from the support tube (`SupportTubeFinite.lean`, `SupportTube.lean`) and the rank as a
32	sum of the per-piece ranks (`Module.rankAtStalk_pi`).
33	
34	This is a genuine reduction, not a repackaging: the hypothesis it trades for is the
35	*geometric separation* of the chosen pieces, which the tube produces one base point at a
36	time, whereas the discharged hypotheses were fibrewise flatness statements over a
37	nonreduced base.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'` — the equalizer
42	  collapses over an arbitrary base ring (the field-level lemma generalized).
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated` — the Čech
44	  difference vanishes.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated` — the certificate from
46	  (c1) plus a rank reading, with no kernel-spanning and no flatness input.
47	-/

63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
64	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
65	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
66	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
67	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)

71	/-- On the diagonal the two overlap-restriction maps coincide: the two `≤`-witnesses
72	`pieces i ⊓ pieces i ≤ pieces i` are definitionally equal (proof irrelevance).  The
73	base-ring form of `DivisorFamilyFieldDegree`'s field-level lemma. -/
74	lemma toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' (i : A.index) :
75	    A.toOvlLeft i i = A.toOvlRight i i :=
76	  rfl
77	
78	/-- **Support separation collapses the equalizer to the whole product, over any base
79	ring.** If the overlap colength modules vanish off the diagonal, every element of the
80	product of chart-local colengths satisfies the equalizer condition.
81	
82	The field-level statement (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated`) never used invertibility;
83	this is the same argument over `R`, which is what the DD-R gate consumes. -/
84	lemma gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'
85	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
86	    A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤ := by
87	  refine eq_top_iff.mpr fun s _ => ?_
88	  rw [mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
89	  rintro ⟨i, j⟩
90	  by_cases hij : i = j
91	  · subst hij
92	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i i => (f : _ → _))
93	      (A.toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' i)) (s i)
94	  · haveI := hsep i j hij
95	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
96	
97	/-- **The Čech difference vanishes for a support-separated adaptation.** Its kernel is the
98	whole product, and a linear map whose kernel is everything is zero. -/
99	lemma deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated
100	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
101	    A.deltaLeft = A.deltaRight := by
102	  have h : A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 := by
103	    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_top]
104	    exact A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
105	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp h
106	
107	/-- The equalizer, as a module, is the whole product of chart-local colengths. -/
108	noncomputable def gluedTopEquiv' (h : A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤) : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd :=
109	  (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ h).trans Submodule.topEquiv
110	
111	/-! ## The two flat-cokernel clauses, for free -/
112	
113	/-- (c3) for a support-separated adaptation: the cokernel of `W(d) ↪ ∏_j colength j` is the
114	zero module, because the inclusion is onto. -/
115	lemma flat_coker_incl_of_separated
116	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
117	    Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) := by
118	  haveI : Subsingleton (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) := by
119	    rw [A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep]
120	    infer_instance
121	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv
122	    (N := A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) (M := PUnit.{u+1})
123	    (LinearEquiv.ofSubsingleton _ _)
124	
125	/-- (c4) for a support-separated adaptation: the Čech difference is the zero map, so its
126	range is `⊥` and the cokernel is the overlap product itself — flat as soon as the overlap
127	product is.  In the seed setting that flatness is already landed
128	(`flat_ovlProd_of_seed`). -/
129	lemma flat_coker_diff_of_separated [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
130	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
131	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)) := by
132	  have hzero : A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 :=
133	    sub_eq_zero.mpr (A.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated hsep)
134	  rw [hzero, LinearMap.range_zero]
135	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot ⊥ rfl)
136	
137	/-! ## Separation is a statement about the support, not about the equations
138	
139	The hypothesis `hsep` above is checkable geometrically: an overlap whose points all avoid
140	the family support carries a unit equation, hence a unit overlap ideal, hence a vanishing
141	overlap colength.  In particular an adaptation in which **at most one piece meets the
142	support** is automatically separated. -/
143	
144	/-- **Overlaps that miss the support are separated.** If no point of `pieces i ⊓ pieces j`
145	lies in the support locus, then `A.eqn i` restricts to a unit there (its germ is a unit at
146	every point, `RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), so the overlap ideal is the unit ideal
147	and the overlap colength vanishes. -/
148	lemma subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (i j : A.index)
149	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
150	    Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
151	  have hunit : IsUnit (relResAlgHom C R
152	      (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)) := by
153	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply]
154	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
155	    intro z hz
156	    rw [(relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
157	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
158	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff i hz.1).mpr
159	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
160	  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ :=
161	    Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)) hunit
162	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr htop
163	
164	/-- **One support-meeting piece suffices.** If every piece other than `j₀` avoids the
165	support entirely, the adaptation is separated: any off-diagonal overlap involves a piece
166	missing the support, so the overlap misses it too. -/
167	lemma forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece (j₀ : A.index)
168	    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
169	      ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
170	    ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
171	  intro i j hij
172	  refine A.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus i j fun z hz => ?_
173	  by_cases hi : i = j₀
174	  · exact hother j (by rw [← hi]; exact fun h => hij h.symm) z hz.2
175	  · exact hother i hi z hz.1
176	
177	/-! ## The certificate -/
178	
179	/-- **The certificate of a support-separated adaptation.** With the off-diagonal overlap
180	colengths vanishing, the equalizer is the whole product, the Čech difference is zero, and
181	both flat-cokernel clauses hold automatically.  What is left is exactly the (c1) data —
182	each chart-local colength finite projective over `R` — plus the constant-rank reading,
183	which for the product is the sum of the per-piece ranks.
184	
185	This is the shape the pointwise gate can consume: no kernel-spanning hypothesis, and no
186	flatness of a Čech cokernel over a possibly nonreduced base. -/
187	theorem isCertified_of_separated {n : ℕ} [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
188	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
189	    (hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
190	    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
191	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
192	      ∑ᶠ j : A.index, Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) (A.colength j) p = n) :
193	    A.IsCertified n := by
194	  classical
195	  haveI := hfin
196	  haveI := hproj
197	  haveI : ∀ j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) := fun _ =>
198	    Module.Flat.of_projective
199	  have htop := A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
200	  have hequiv : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd := A.gluedTopEquiv' htop
201	  haveI hprodProj : Module.Projective R A.chartProd :=
202	    Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.chartProd)
203	      (DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype R A.index (fun j => A.colength j))
204	  refine
205	    { finite_colength := hfin
206	      projective_colength := hproj
207	      finite_glued := Module.Finite.equiv hequiv.symm
208	      projective_glued := Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.Glued) hequiv.symm
209	      rankAtStalk_glued := fun p => ?_
210	      flat_coker_incl := A.flat_coker_incl_of_separated hsep
211	      flat_coker_diff := A.flat_coker_diff_of_separated hsep }
212	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv hequiv, Module.rankAtStalk_pi]
213	  exact hrank p
214	
215	end DivisorAdaptation

12	# The support tube: the family support is closed over the base (DDR-4 finiteness input)
13	
14	The geometric half of the DDR-4 certificate clause (c1) (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3
15	item 4): for a local-equation system `d` on a scheme `X`, the **support locus** — the
16	set of points where the (well-defined, by the ratio law) germ of the local equation is
17	not a unit — is closed in `X`; over a base `S` with `X → S` universally closed (the
18	standing `IsProper C.hom`, base-changed to the relative curve over every test ring),
19	its image in `S` is closed, and the **tube lemma** holds: if the support fibre over a
20	base point `s` is contained in an open `U` (e.g. a union of adaptation pieces), then so
21	is the whole support over a Zariski neighbourhood of `s` — piece isolation Zariski-locally
22	on the base.
23	
24	## Main declarations
25	
26	* `IsClosedMap.exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset` — the topological tube core: a
27	  closed map, a closed set `T`, an open `U` containing the `T`-fibre over `y` ⟹ an open
28	  neighbourhood `V ∋ y` with `f⁻¹(V) ∩ T ⊆ U` (via `Set.kernImage`);
29	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.unitLocus` / `supportLocus` — the (open) locus where the
30	  equations are germwise units, and its closed complement;
31	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ` — membership reads on ANY
32	  covering member through the ratio law;
33	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLocus_inter_opens` — the per-member trace
34	  `supp ∩ U_x = U_x \ D(eqn x)`;
35	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_image_supportLocus`,
36	  `Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube` — closed image and the tube, for any
37	  `f : X ⟶ S` with `[UniversallyClosed f]`;
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperRelSndLeft`, `instIsProperRelCurveHom` — **the
39	  licence**: `IsProper C.hom` base-changes to the relative curve over an arbitrary test
40	  ring `R` (the field-keyed instances of `Curve/BaseChangeInstances` generalised), so
41	  `UniversallyClosed (relCurve C R ↘ Spec R)` fires by resolution;
42	* `DivisorAdaptation.mem_basicOpen_eqn_of_mem_unitLocus` / `unitLocus_eq` /
43	  `supportLocus_inter_pieces` — the adaptation reads the SAME support: on a piece,
44	  `d`'s support trace is `D(h_j) \ D(f_j)` (through `eqn_rel`, both ways);
45	* `FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces` — the pieces' section rings are `R`-flat;
46	* `DivisorAdaptation.flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` /
47	  `projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` — **the (c1) junction**: a
48	  fibrewise-regular adaptation equation has flat colength over the Noetherian test
49	  ring (the `SlicingFlat` keystone on the piece ring), and a finite colength (the
50	  support-tube finiteness input) is then projective — the two clauses of

52	-/

66	variable {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]

68	/-- **The closed-map tube lemma**: for a closed map `f`, a closed `T ⊆ X` and an open
69	`U ⊆ X`, if the `T`-fibre over `y` is contained in `U` then so is `f⁻¹(V) ∩ T` for some
70	open neighbourhood `V` of `y`. Take `V := Set.kernImage f (U ∪ Tᶜ)`, open by
71	`isClosedMap_iff_kernImage`. -/
72	theorem IsClosedMap.exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset {f : X → Y}
73	    (hf : IsClosedMap f) {T U : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (hU : IsOpen U) {y : Y}
74	    (hfib : f ⁻¹' {y} ∩ T ⊆ U) :
75	    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ y ∈ V ∧ f ⁻¹' V ∩ T ⊆ U := by
76	  refine ⟨Set.kernImage f (U ∪ Tᶜ),
77	    isClosedMap_iff_kernImage.mp hf (hU.union hT.isOpen_compl), ?_, ?_⟩
78	  · intro x hx
79	    by_cases hxT : x ∈ T
80	    · exact Or.inl (hfib ⟨hx, hxT⟩)
81	    · exact Or.inr hxT
82	  · rintro x ⟨hxV, hxT⟩
83	    rcases hxV (rfl : f x = f x) with h | h
84	    · exact h
85	    · exact absurd hxT h
86	
87	end TubeCore

93	/-! ## The support locus of a local-equation system -/
94	
95	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
96	
97	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : X.LocalEquations)
98	
99	/-- **The unit locus** of a local-equation system: the (open) union of the basic opens
100	of the equations — the locus where the divisor cut by `d` is trivial. -/
101	def unitLocus : X.Opens := ⨆ x, X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)
102	
103	lemma basicOpen_le_unitLocus (x : X) : X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) ≤ d.unitLocus :=
104	  le_iSup (fun x => X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)) x
105	
106	/-- Membership in the unit locus reads on ANY covering member containing the point:
107	`y ∈ unitLocus` iff the germ of `eqn x` at `y` is a unit, for every member `x` with
108	`y ∈ cover.opens x` (well-definedness across members is the ratio law). -/
109	lemma mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
110	    y ∈ d.unitLocus
111	      ↔ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) := by
112	  constructor
113	  · intro h
114	    obtain ⟨x', hx'⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp h
115	    have hy' : y ∈ d.cover.opens x' := X.basicOpen_le _ hx'
116	    have hu' : IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x') y hy').hom (d.eqn x')) :=
117	      (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy').mp hx'
118	    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := d.ratio_isUnit x x'
119	    have hyW : y ∈ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x' := ⟨hy, hy'⟩
120	    have h := congrArg
121	      ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x') y hyW).hom) hu
122	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
123	    rw [h, IsUnit.mul_iff]
124	    exact ⟨u.isUnit.map _, hu'⟩
125	  · intro h
126	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨x, (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr h⟩
127	
128	/-- **The support locus** of a local-equation system: the closed set of points where
129	the (well-defined) germ of the local equation fails to be a unit — the underlying set
130	of the divisor cut by `d`. -/
131	def supportLocus : Set X := (d.unitLocus : Set X)ᶜ
132	
133	lemma isClosed_supportLocus : IsClosed d.supportLocus :=
134	  d.unitLocus.isOpen.isClosed_compl
135	
136	lemma mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
137	    y ∈ d.supportLocus
138	      ↔ ¬ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) :=
139	  not_congr (d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy)
140	
141	/-- **The per-member trace of the support**: on a covering member, the support locus is
142	the member minus the basic open of its equation. -/
143	lemma supportLocus_inter_opens (x : X) :
144	    d.supportLocus ∩ (d.cover.opens x : Set X)
145	      = (d.cover.opens x : Set X) \ (X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) : Set X) := by
146	  ext y
147	  constructor
148	  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hy⟩
149	    refine ⟨hy, fun hyb => hsupp (d.basicOpen_le_unitLocus x hyb)⟩
150	  · rintro ⟨hy, hyb⟩
151	    refine ⟨fun hyU => hyb ?_, hy⟩
152	    exact (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy).mp hyU)
153	
154	/-- **The support is closed over the base**: the image of the support locus under a
155	universally closed morphism (e.g. the structure morphism of the relative curve, from
156	the standing `IsProper C.hom`) is closed. -/
157	theorem isClosed_image_supportLocus (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] :
158	    IsClosed (f.base '' d.supportLocus) :=
159	  f.isClosedMap _ d.isClosed_supportLocus
160	
161	/-- **The support tube** (piece isolation, Zariski-locally on the base): for a
162	universally closed `f : X ⟶ S`, if the support fibre over a base point `s` is contained
163	in an open `U` (a union of adaptation pieces, in the DDR-4 instantiation), then there
164	is a Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `s` such that the whole support over `V` is contained
165	in `U`. -/
166	theorem exists_supportTube (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X}
167	    (hU : IsOpen U) {s : S} (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
168	    ∃ V : S.Opens, s ∈ V ∧ f.base ⁻¹' (V : Set S) ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
169	  obtain ⟨V, hVopen, hsV, hV⟩ := (f.isClosedMap).exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset
170	    d.isClosed_supportLocus hU hfib
171	  exact ⟨⟨V, hVopen⟩, hsV, hV⟩
172	
173	end Scheme.LocalEquations

182	/-- **Base change of properness to an arbitrary test ring**: the second projection of
183	`C ⊗ Spec R` is proper, for every commutative `k`-algebra `R` — the general-`R` form of
184	`Curve/BaseChangeInstances.instIsProperSndLeft` (which is keyed on field extensions).
185	This is the DDR-4 support-tube licence over the `Z(♦)`-chart rings `R_Z`. -/
186	instance instIsProperRelSndLeft : IsProper (snd C (overSpec k R)).left :=
187	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsProper)
188	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k R)) inferInstance
189	
190	/-- The properness instance, keyed on the `relCurve C R ↘ Spec R` spelling installed by
191	`relCurve.instOver` (definitionally the second projection). In particular
192	`UniversallyClosed (relCurve C R ↘ Spec R)` fires by resolution, which is what
193	`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube` consumes. -/
194	instance instIsProperRelCurveHom :
195	    IsProper ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) :=
196	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper (snd C (overSpec k R)).left)

198	/-- Acceptance smoke test: the support tube applies to the relative curve over an
199	arbitrary test ring with the universally-closed instance found by resolution. -/
200	private theorem supportTube_smoke (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
201	    {U : Set (relCurve C R)} (hU : IsOpen U) {s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R)}
202	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus
203	      ⊆ U) :
204	    ∃ V : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).Opens, s ∈ V ∧
205	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' (V : Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)))
206	        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U :=
207	  d.exists_supportTube _ hU hfib
